findings.claim: All HTTP 403 responses from Keto checks are treated and cached as authorization denials, which can silently mask service/authentication misconfiguration as a normal object denial.
findings.evidence: The check path now returns `Ok(false)` and caches `false` whenever `resp.status() == reqwest::StatusCode::FORBIDDEN` without parsing or validating the expected `{"allowed": false}` denial body; the acceptance/global rule requires authority failure to fail closed, and the constraints call out silent failure as a review target.
findings.suggested_fix: For 403, parse the response body as the expected Keto denial shape and only return `Ok(false)` when it is a valid denied check; otherwise return `PortError::Transport` or `PortError::Serialization` so authority-service failures terminate rather than look like ordinary denials.
